subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Increasing the bit depth (resolution) of audio sampling improves:
options: The accuracy of each recorded amplitude value
The number of samples per second
questions.explain: More bits per sample give finer amplitude resolution, more accurately representing each sample.

questions.q: A key advantage of Unicode (e.g. UTF-8/UTF-16) over ASCII is that it:
options: Uses fewer bits per character in all cases
Cannot represent the original ASCII characters
Can represent characters from a vast range of languages and symbols
Stores numbers more efficiently than binary
questions.explain: Unicode provides code points for characters across the world's writing systems, far beyond ASCII's set.

questions.q: Adding the 8-bit two's complement numbers 01111111 and 00000001 produces an incorrect result because of:
questions.explain: 127 + 1 should be 128, but the result wraps to 10000000 (-128): a positive overflow.

questions.q: Which property distinguishes hashing from encryption?
options: Hashing is a one-way function that cannot be reversed to recover the original input
Hashing requires a public and private key pair
Hashing always produces a longer output than its input
Hashing guarantees the message stays confidential during transmission
questions.explain: Hashing is a one-way function producing a fixed-size digest that cannot be reversed to the original data.

questions.q: Increasing the colour (bit) depth of an image increases:
options: The frame rate of the image
The number of pixels in the image
The number of distinct colours each pixel can represent and the file size
questions.explain: Greater bit depth allows more colours per pixel (2^n) but increases the file size.

questions.q: In an 8-bit two's complement representation, what is the value of 11111000?
questions.explain: As an 8-bit two's complement number, 11111000 = -8 (invert and add one: 00001000 = 8).

questions.q: A bitwise OR operation is commonly used to:
options: Set specific bits to 1 using a mask
Test whether two bits are equal
questions.explain: OR with a mask sets the masked bit positions to 1 while leaving others unchanged.

questions.q: Run-length encoding (RLE) is most effective when data contains:
options: Highly random data with no repetition
Many long runs of repeated identical values
questions.explain: RLE replaces consecutive repeated values with a count and value, so it works best on long runs.

questions.q: Applying a bitwise AND with the mask 00001111 to a byte will:
options: Set the upper four bits and clear the lower four
Shift the bits left by four
Clear (zero) the upper four bits and keep the lower four
questions.explain: AND with 00001111 keeps the lower nibble unchanged and forces the upper nibble to 0.

questions.q: In digital sound, the sampling rate (frequency) refers to:
options: The number of samples taken per second
The number of bits used per sample
questions.explain: Sampling rate is how many amplitude samples are captured per second, measured in Hz.

questions.q: In a two's complement number, the most significant bit:
options: Always represents a positive power of two
questions.explain: In two's complement the MSB carries a negative weight (e.g. -128 in 8 bits), which is why it indicates sign.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal representation of the binary number 11011110?
questions.explain: 1101 = D and 1110 = E, giving 0xDE.

questions.q: A normalised binary floating-point mantissa (two's complement) for a positive number begins with:
questions.explain: A normalised positive two's complement mantissa starts 0.1..., i.e. the first two bits are 01.

questions.q: A disadvantage of sign-and-magnitude representation compared with two's complement is that:
options: It has two representations of zero and complicates arithmetic
questions.explain: Sign-and-magnitude has both +0 and -0 and makes addition/subtraction harder, unlike two's complement.

questions.q: What is the denary (decimal) value of the binary number 10110101?
In symmetric encryption:
options: Different keys are used to encrypt and decrypt
The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
The public key encrypts and a different private key is published
questions.explain: Symmetric encryption uses a single shared secret key for both encryption and decryption.

questions.q: In floating-point representation, the exponent primarily determines:
questions.explain: The exponent scales the mantissa and so governs the range/magnitude of values that can be represented.

questions.q: Huffman coding achieves compression by:
options: Assigning shorter codes to more frequent symbols and longer codes to rarer ones
Replacing repeated runs with a single byte
Discarding the least significant bits of each value
Encrypting the data with a key
questions.explain: Huffman coding uses variable-length, prefix-free codes, giving frequent symbols shorter bit patterns.

questions.q: What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of -20?
A logical left shift of an unsigned binary number by one place is equivalent to:
questions.explain: Shifting left by one place multiplies an unsigned binary value by two (the LSB becomes 0).

questions.q: Floating-point underflow occurs when a number is:
options: Too large in magnitude to store
Too small in magnitude (too close to zero) to be represented
questions.explain: Underflow happens when a value is too small in magnitude for the exponent range to represent.

questions.q: Which statement about lossless compression is correct?
options: It can only be used on text files
Some original data is permanently discarded
The original data can be perfectly reconstructed from the compressed file
It always achieves higher ratios than lossy compression
questions.explain: Lossless compression allows exact reconstruction of the original data with no information lost.

questions.q: Normalisation of a floating-point number is performed mainly to:
options: Maximise the precision by removing leading redundant digits in the mantissa
questions.explain: Normalisation adjusts the mantissa to its most significant form, maximising precision for the available bits.

questions.q: In asymmetric (public-key) encryption, a message encrypted with a recipient's public key can be decrypted using:
questions.explain: Data encrypted with the public key can only be decrypted with the matching private key.

questions.q: The Vernam cipher (one-time pad) is theoretically unbreakable provided the key is:
options: Shorter than the message and reused
Truly random, at least as long as the message, used only once and kept secret
A simple shift of three letters
questions.explain: A Vernam cipher is perfectly secure only with a truly random key as long as the message, used once and kept secret.

questions.q: For a fixed total word length, increasing the number of mantissa bits (at the expense of exponent bits) will:
questions.explain: More mantissa bits give greater precision, but fewer exponent bits reduce the available range.

questions.q: How many distinct characters can the standard 7-bit ASCII code represent?
questions.explain: 7 bits give 2^7 = 128 distinct codes.

questions.q: Rounding errors in floating-point arithmetic arise mainly because:
options: Many real values cannot be represented exactly in a finite number of bits
questions.explain: Finite mantissa bits mean many real numbers must be approximated, introducing rounding error.

questions.q: The Nyquist theorem states that to accurately reconstruct a signal, the sampling rate must be at least:
options: Equal to the highest frequency present
Twice the highest frequency present in the signal
questions.explain: Nyquist requires sampling at a minimum of twice the highest frequency component to avoid aliasing.
